messages.text: Masters, Webb criticise FIFA over Balogun red card controversy

metadata.summary: Two of the most powerful men in English football have joined forces to hit out at FIFA and the U-turn which allowed USA striker Folarin Balogun to play on at the World Cup last month, despite the red card which should have led to an automatic ban.
metadata.content: Richard Masters and Howard Webb criticise FIFA over Folarin Balogun's red card controversy at 2026 World Cup | Football News | Sky Sports Skip to content Richard Masters and Howard Webb criticise FIFA over Folarin Balogun's red card controversy at 2026 World Cup USA striker Folarin Balogun had a red card suspended at the World Cup; it caused huge controversy after Donald Trump had called Gianni Infantino ahead of the last 32 match against Belgium; Balogun was sent off against Bosnia & Herzegovina and was suspended for two games Rob Dorsett Football Correspondent @RobDorsettSky Wednesday 19 August 2026 18:01, UK Image: Folarin Balogun was sent off against Bosnia & Herzegovina - but had his two-game ban controversially suspended Two of the most powerful men in English football have joined forces to hit out at FIFA and the U-turn which allowed USA striker Folarin Balogun to play on at the World Cup last month, despite the red card which should have led to an automatic ban. Richard Masters , the chief executive of the Premier League and Howard Webb , the chief refereeing officer in England, say the decision undermines faith in football at all levels of the game. Balogun was sent off in the last 32 match against Bosnia & Herzegovina which led to an automatic ban under World Cup rules, without the opportunity for appeal, or for the ban to be reduced. messages.text: Item surprises big two for Juddmonte International glory

metadata.summary: Item delivered for Andrew Balding and the sponsors to land a 10-1 surprise in the Juddmonte International at York – with the big two of Constitution River and Ombudsman only third and fourth respectively.
metadata.content: Item surprises big two for Juddmonte International glory | Racing News | Sky Sports Skip to content Item surprises big two for Juddmonte International glory We were treated to another epic renewal of the Juddmonte International on Wednesday but it was far from the match-race that it was built up to be, with Item delivered late to deny Almaqam in a thrilling finish to the York feature. Wednesday 19 August 2026 17:00, UK Image: Item ridden by Colin Keane on their way to winning the Juddmonte International Stakes Item delivered for Andrew Balding and the sponsors to land a 10-1 surprise in the Juddmonte International at York – with the big two of Constitution River and Ombudsman only third and fourth respectively. Hawk Mountain rather unexpectedly set the early pace, with stablemate Constitution River tucked in keenly behind him and odds-on favourite Ombudsman at the rear under William Buick, kept company by another Aidan O'Brien runner, Action. Hawk Mountain was still in front as they moved to the top of the long Knavesmire straight, with Buick beginning to make headway on the inside rail, as Ryan Moore and Constitution River kicked for home over two furlongs out. Ombudsman kept making ground on the inside, but the dangers were coming on the outside and it was Ed Walker's Almaqam who pulled away with half a furlong to run, only for Item to arrive in full flight, just getting his head down on the line in the hands of Colin Keane. messages.text: Arsenal agree £51m deal to sign Aston Villa's Konsa

metadata.summary: Arsenal have agreed a £51m deal to sign Ezri Konsa from Aston Villa.
metadata.content: Ezri Konsa transfer news: Arsenal agree deal with Aston Villa to sign England defender | Football News | Sky Sports Skip to content Transfer Ezri Konsa transfer news: Arsenal agree deal with Aston Villa to sign England defender Ezri Konsa has two years remaining on his Aston Villa contract; Arsenal also held an interest in Jarell Quansah but look set to move for Konsa; Arsenal currently have William Saliba and Jurrien Timber out injured By Adrian Kajumba and Lyall Thomas Wednesday 19 August 2026 18:12, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Watch Ezri Konsa's best moments for Aston Villa last season Arsenal have agreed a £51m deal to sign Ezri Konsa from Aston Villa. The Premier League champions have been looking for a new defender with William Saliba out for an extended period of time and Jurrien Timber also sidelined with a long-term groin problem. Arsenal looked into a potential deal for Bayer Leverkusen's Jarell Quansah but have chosen to advance with a move for his England team-mate Konsa. Both players have a similar profile and can play at right-back and centre-back. Villa had initially held out for £60m, with Arsenal hoping to pay much less, but the two clubs found a compromise on Thursday to strike a deal for the 28-year-old. messages.text: Sainz signs multi-year contract extension with Williams

metadata.summary: Carlos Sainz has signed a multi-year contract extension with Williams that will keep him with the team for the 2027 Formula 1 season and beyond.
metadata.content: Carlos Sainz: Williams driver signs multi-year contract extension to remain with team for 2027 F1 season and beyond | F1 News | Sky Sports Skip to content Carlos Sainz: Williams driver signs multi-year contract extension to remain with team for 2027 F1 season and beyond Carlos Sainz signs multi-year extension with Williams; announcement follows team-mate Alex Albon signing extension a day earlier; watch the Dutch Grand Prix Sprint weekend live on Sky Sports F1 from Friday Wednesday 19 August 2026 15:41, UK Image: Carlos Sainz has signed a multi-year contract extension with Williams Carlos Sainz has signed a multi-year contract extension with Williams that will keep him with the team for the 2027 Formula 1 season and beyond. The 31-year-old Spaniard had expressed doubt over his future with Williams amid a second campaign with the team that has failed to deliver the strong results of 2025, which makes his decision to sign a multi-year deal something of a surprise. Wednesday's announcement came a day after the team confirmed Sainz's team-mate Alex Albon had signed a one-year extension to remain with the team for the 2027 season, with both drivers' previous deals having been set to expire at the end of 2026.
